info.title: NeuroCal API
info.description: Generated from packages/contracts (Zod). Do not edit by hand: change the contract and run `npm run openapi`.

servers.description: Local backend (`npm run dev` in backend)

get.description: 404 until the profile has been set up.

delete.description: Removes the profile, meals, check-ins, scores, imported sleep and screen time, meal photos, any waitlist entry for the email, and the sign-in. It cannot be undone.

put.description: The first save creates the profile and needs displayName, dietaryPreference, dailyCalorieTarget and macroTargets. Later saves can be partial.

get.summary: Get a day's intake against its targets

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: Calendar day in the user's time zone, e.g. 2026-09-29. Defaults to today.

post.summary: Get a short-lived URL to upload a meal photo to
post.description: PUT the photo's bytes to `uploadUrl` with exactly the returned `headers`, then pass `photoKey` to POST /meals/analyze. The photo must be an image of at most 8 MB, and the bytes sent must match `sizeBytes`.

post.summary: Propose food items from a meal photo
post.description: Send the `photoKey` of an uploaded photo as JSON, or the photo itself as multipart. Nothing is saved. A photo that can't be read is a normal 200 response with `problem` set.

photo.description: The meal photo (JPEG, PNG, WebP or HEIC).

post.description: One per day in the profile's time zone; logging the same day again replaces it. Kilograms.

get.summary: Weigh-ins with the trend and goal progress
get.description: The trend is an exponential moving average that evens out day-to-day water swings; goal progress and the projected date are read from it, not from single weigh-ins.

parameters.name: days
parameters.description: How many days back, 1–730. Defaults to 90.

get.summary: Where you are in your fast
get.description: Worked out from logged meals: a fast runs from the last meal, and the eating window opens with the first meal after a full fast. The protocol comes from the bio-profile; people who answered the weight goal's safety question get 12:12 at most.

Each cup with its time, add-ins, caffeine and calories, whether it came after the caffeine curfew (eight hours after waking) and whether it ended a fast; the day's caffeine and the add-ins' calories, which count toward the day.

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: A date like 2026-10-23; today in your time zone when left out.

post.description: Not a meal. Black coffee, espresso, fat (MCT oil, butter, ghee) and creatine keep a fast going, as a 'fat fast'; milk, sugar or collagen end it. The add-ins' calories count toward the day. Caffeine after the curfew lowers the next day's evening timing in the Focus Score.

put.description: Fast until a time, for a day without meals or a longer fast. It counts from the last meal, must end at least half an hour ahead and last no more than planLimitHours (48, or 12 at the cautious protocol; none when pregnant or with an eating-disorder history). Logging a meal ends it; water, black coffee and plain tea (under 10 kcal) don't.

delete.description: The timer goes back to counting from meals and the protocol.

post.description: A 2-minute reaction-time test after the Psychomotor Vigilance Task: send each reaction in milliseconds and the number of taps before the light. The API scores it (0–100) from the median, lapses (500 ms or more) and false starts. A self-check for comparing your own days, not a medical test.

get.description: Newest first, with your usual score: the median of the checks before the latest, once there are three.

parameters.name: days
parameters.description: How many days back, 1–365. Defaults to 30.

post.description: Calories are burned above resting (MET − 1) × kg × hours, from the latest weigh-in, or 70 kg without one.

get.summary: Get a day's exercise with its totals

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: Calendar day in the user's time zone, e.g. 2026-09-29. Defaults to today.

get.description: The day's mean US AQI for the town you set (Open-Meteo), your environment check (morning daylight, a dark and quiet bedroom, filtered water), and the Focus Score's environment input.

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: Calendar day in the user's time zone, e.g. 2026-09-29. Defaults to today.

put.summary: Set the town for air quality
put.description: A town or postcode, looked up once and stored rounded to about 10 km. Null clears it.
Items not sent keep their answer. Default date: today.

get.description: Levels 1 (Aware) to 5 (Upgraded) from habits kept over the last 28 days: logging, food quality, evening rhythm and fasting, sleep, stress and Brain speed, then movement. Each level needs every one below it. Each habit says how close it is.

post.description: Names already there, ignoring case and plurals, are skipped. Returns the whole pantry.

get.description: 404 until a plan has been made.

post.description: 1 to 3 days of meals sized to your calorie and macro targets, using your pantry first and fitting your fasting plan (one meal for OMAD, two for 16:8, else three). Meals come from Claude (schema-checked); calories use USDA catalog values where ingredients match. The shopping list combines everything not in your pantry. Replaces the last plan.

Ingredients are read (Claude, schema-checked) and converted to grams. Those that match the food catalog use its USDA FoodData Central values scaled by weight; the rest use estimates, and each ingredient says which. Per serving, with the dish graded by its most processed ingredient. Nothing is saved.

Send the list as JSON `text`, or a photo of a written list, receipt or shopping app as multipart `photo`. Each item is graded (whole, processed, ultra-processed) and marked keep, swap (with a cleaner choice) or limit. Kitchen devices are suggested only when the list shows a swap they make easy, from enabled catalog products. Nothing is saved.

photo.description: A photo of the list (JPEG, PNG or WebP).

post.description: Up to three recipes built mostly from your pantry, sized to the calories and macros left today and your dietary preference. Needs at least three items. Each ingredient says whether it's already in your pantry. Nothing is saved.

get.description: Each supplement with today's tick and days of the bottle left, plus checks no single label can show: daily totals across products against adult upper limits, the same nutrient in several products, and caffeine taken in the evening.

post.summary: Add a supplement to your stack
post.description: Usually straight from a label scan. At most 30 supplements.

put.summary: Change servings, timing or the bottle size

delete.summary: Remove a supplement from your stack

put.summary: Tick a supplement as taken today

get.description: As last reported by RevenueCat. Without access it asks RevenueCat directly once, so a purchase made seconds ago already counts. When the paywall is on, photo and label reading and recipe suggestions answer 402 `subscription_required` without access.

About 100 everyday and brain-friendly foods, per serving, with the goals and diets each suits, then chain-restaurant menu items (`category: "eating_out"`, with `chain`, `regions` and `betterPick`). Nutrition comes from USDA FoodData Central (`fdcId`). Small enough to fetch once and search on the device.

post.description: 1–4 photos of the same package (nutrition panel, ingredients, dates), as uploaded photoKeys or multipart `photo` fields. NeuroCal grades the ingredient list (NOVA: whole, processed, ultra-processed, naming the industrial ingredients) and flags added sugar, sodium and best-before dates. Nothing is saved.

get.description: From Open Food Facts (Open Database License: credit it where the data shows), graded the same way as a label scan. 404 when the barcode isn't in the database: photograph the label instead.

post.summary: A better choice for a processed food
post.description: Send the scanned food's name, ingredients and level. NeuroCal finds the industrial ingredients itself, then says what a cleaner shop-bought version lists and gives the same food made at home, built mostly from your pantry, with each ingredient marked if you have it. A kitchen device is shown only when the recipe's steps use one, from enabled catalog products. Nothing is saved.

post.summary: Read a supplement label from 1–4 photos
post.description: Photos of the same bottle from different sides are read as one label, so a label that wraps around the bottle comes out whole. Upload each photo as for meals (POST /uploads/meal-photo) and pass the photoKeys, or send them as multipart/form-data, one `photo` field per photo. Returns what the label says, flags such as proprietary blends, doses above upper limits, missing third-party testing and expiry, and a close own-brand alternative when there is one. It reports the label only and is not a safety or quality verdict. Nothing is saved.

get.summary: List a day's meals, earliest first

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: Calendar day in the user's time zone, e.g. 2026-09-29. Defaults to today.

get.summary: Suggest recipes for the current bio-state
Get a day's Focus Score with its inputs and explanation

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: Calendar day in the user's time zone, e.g. 2026-09-29. Defaults to today.

get.summary: Get everything the Today screen shows in one call
get.description: Without `date`: today, with suggestions, fasting, the supplement stack and Brain speed. With a past `date`: that day's score, calories and meals only. An extra that fails is left out rather than failing the call.

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: Calendar day in the user's time zone, e.g. 2026-09-29. Defaults to today.

get.summary: Get the last N days, oldest first

parameters.name: days
parameters.description: How many days, ending today. Defaults to 7.

get.summary: Suggest protocols and products for the week's weak points
List every product for the admin screen
get.description: Admins only; anyone else gets 403.

post.summary: Add a product from the admin screen
post.description: Admins only. An affiliate or own-brand product needs a link.

put.summary: Change a product's link, affiliate label or on/off state
put.description: Admins only. Send only the fields to change; `url: null` goes back to the catalog's link.

delete.summary: Remove a product added from the admin screen
delete.description: Admins only. Catalog products can't be removed, only turned off.

post.description: A session replaces any stored session from the same source that overlaps it. Sleep must end after it starts, last at most 24 hours and not end in the future.
Samples upsert on source and windowStart. Minutes can't exceed the window length.

get.description: Admins only. Newest first, each video with the techniques taken from its transcript and their review status.

post.description: Admins only. With a transcript, techniques are taken from it at once (Claude, schema-checked); without one, it waits in the list. Transcripts aren't stored.

post.summary: Add a transcript to a video in the list
post.description: Admins only. Takes techniques from it for review.

put.description: Admins only. Approving adds it to the catalog as a routine (optionally edited), tagged by pillar and linked to the moment in the video; it is then matched to people's weak points.

post.summary: Check watched channels for new videos now
post.description: Admins only. Needs YOUTUBE_API_KEY; titles and links only.

get.description: The last 14 days with a glucose-sensor summary: average, time in range (70–140 and 70–180 mg/dL) and variability.

post.description: Daily summaries the app works out from Health Connect / Apple Health samples (only days with about 12 hours or more of sensor readings). When yesterday has one, the Focus Score's blood-sugar input is measured from it: time in range (70–180 with diabetes, else 70–140), less a little for large swings.

get.description: Each marker with readings in the last 400 days: the latest reading, the change against the reading closest to 90 days earlier, whether that went the healthier way, and up to 12 recent points. References are general adult ranges in plain words, never a diagnosis.

post.description: From the app (typed in) or imported from Health Connect / Apple Health. A reading with the same marker, time and source is kept once, so imports can be sent again. Values outside each marker's plausible range are refused.

get.description: Monday to today in the user's time zone: easy cardio minutes, strength and hard sessions, protein days, the ultra-processed share, a steady wake time and morning daylight, each against its weekly target. Health conditions can leave a habit out (skipped, with the reason).

get.summary: Kitchen devices found by the monthly scout
get.description: Admins only. Each kitchen category the shopping review can suggest (air fryer, water filter, ice cream maker, blender) is searched once a month; devices found wait here as pending.

put.description: Admins only. Approving adds it as a product (optionally edited), tagged for its category, so the shopping review can suggest it. Not an affiliate link; change that on the product afterwards.

post.description: Admins only. Needs TAVILY_API_KEY. Only links from the search results are kept.

get.summary: See who is on the waitlist
get.description: Admins only; anyone else gets 403. Counts leave out people who unsubscribed; entries are newest first, at most 500.
Admins only. Chain menu items typed in from each chain's published nutrition, for chains whose sites can't be read automatically. They appear in GET /foods after the built-in ones.

post.summary: Add or update an eating-out item
post.description: Admins only. The calories must roughly add up from protein, carbs and fat (4/4/9 kcal a gram); glycemic load is estimated from net carbs. The same chain, item and country updates the existing item.

delete.summary: Remove an eating-out item an admin added
delete.description: Admins only. Built-in items can't be removed.

post.summary: Ask to be emailed when the app is ready
post.description: Public: no sign-in. Answers the same way whether or not the address was already on the list.
Public: no sign-in. Takes the token from the unsubscribe link in a waitlist email; an unknown token is answered the same way.

cognitoIdToken.description: The Cognito ID token of the signed-in user.

Error.description: Any failure. `message` is written for the user and can be shown as is.
